Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada told reporters last week that her husband, who is Black, had been repeatedly stopped by police while driving.

So when the email titled “June Holiday” arrived in thousands of inboxes, they felt a moment of overdue joy.

Police in Vietnam have rescued more than 400 cats in a bust of a cat meat crime ring in Ho Chi Minh City, according to animal welfare groups and local media reports.

More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Blood minerals and memory: the Great Lakes in focus
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa turns to the Great Lakes region. First, a new Global Witness report reveals how coltan is being smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, amid the ongoing conflict in the east, through Rwanda and on to companies worldwide. Then, artist Grada Kilomba discusses her journey to create a unique monument for Paris commemorating the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'Export trade has increased since exiting the EU, it's been a win'
rfi.description: Ten years after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains one of the most contested political decisions in recent British history. Its legacy is increasingly shaped by diverging interpretations of sovereignty and the UK's place in the world. RFI spoke to Brexit supporter Robert Oulds, director of British think tank the Bruges Group, about what has changed.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch will be inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the Republic’s most symbolic ceremonies.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages
rfi.description: Argentina skipper Lionel Messi added another accolade to his otherworldly list of achievements on Monday when he became the record goalscorer at World Cups since the inception of the tournament in 1930

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

rfi.title: France's scorching weekend heat leads to elderly deaths and spate of drownings
rfi.description: The deaths of three elderly people in southwestern France have been linked to the heatwave hitting the country, while authorities have reported an increase in drownings, as people seek relief from the heat in rivers and lakes.

rfi.title: UK's Starmer resigns as prime minister
rfi.description: UK leader Keir Starmer announced his resignation on Monday following months of pressure, kickstarting a process that will see Britain get its seventh prime minister in a decade.

rfi.title: DRC announces free healthcare for all illnesses in Ituri as Ebola gains ground
rfi.description: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the introduction of free healthcare for all diseases in Ituri – a pilot project that authorities hope to extend nationwide. This comes as the country struggles to contain an Ebola outbreak, with confirmed cases now at over 1,000.

rfi.title: Ethiopia’s ruling party wins another large majority in parliament

euronews.title: Nicotine pouch sales surge among young people, watchdog warns
euronews.description: Flavoured, promoted on social media, discreet and unregulated: sales of addictive nicotine pouches are booming among youth. A global tobacco industry watchdog, STOP, warns that this could lead to a new wave of nicotine addiction.

euronews.title: Iceland kills first whales since 2023, resuming whaling
euronews.description: Iceland's Marine and Freshwater Research Institute has recommended that no more than 150 fin whales are caught in the 2026 season.

euronews.description: The arrival of Japan's emperor and empress in Belgium marks a symbolic moment for two countries whose partnership stretches back more than a century and a half.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen to visit Pashinyan in Yerevan to build on Armenia’s pro-EU vote
euronews.description: As the EU rolls out a support package for Armenia, European Commission President von der Leyen is set to meet re-elected Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan after he secured a decisive pro-West mandate from the Armenian people, sources confirmed to Euronews.

euronews.title: UN launches Hormuz evacuation for 11,000 stranded seafarers
euronews.description: The operation follows a peace agreement between the United States and Iran that ended months of conflict and allowed commercial shipping to resume through one of the world's most important maritime routes.

euronews.description: EU officials and Taliban representatives held a technical meeting in Brussels to discuss the return of Afghan nationals in a fresh attempt to ramp up repatriations of migrants without the right to stay in Europe.

euronews.title: From Bolsonaro and Bukele to Fujimori and De la Espriella: Trump and Latin America's rightward turn
euronews.description: Soon after the US president first moved into the White House, his policies and outspoken backing for certain candidates inspired a new wave of Latin American leaders now shaping the continent’s future.

euronews.title: LEGO's Julia Goldin named first-ever European CMO of the Year at Cannes Lions
euronews.description: Chosen by more than 800 marketing leaders from across Europe, Julia Goldin was recognised for helping transform LEGO into a global cultural brand through partnerships spanning entertainment, gaming and sport.

euronews.title: Armenia and Azerbaijan agree landmark internet deal as peace process continues
euronews.description: Armenia and Azerbaijan’s leading telecom companies agreed to a joint internet transit project as both countries move forward together after decades of war, boosting regional connectivity.

euronews.title: Versailles unveils gallery for 250th anniversary of US independence
euronews.description: Opening on Saturday 4 July, this gallery brings together paintings, sculptures and portraits from the château’s collections to spotlight the political, diplomatic and military figures of independence.

euronews.title: How Israel became a test case for the EU's institutional battle over foreign policy
euronews.description: Diverging views on the EU's relations with Israel are exposing a growing rivalry between the European Commission and top diplomat Kaja Kallas over who sets the bloc's foreign policy, undermining its overall coherence.

euronews.title: Spain toughens rules for e-scooters: new requirements
euronews.description: The government has approved a reform to the General Traffic Regulations making helmets compulsory for e-scooter users nationwide and setting a minimum age of 15. The measure forms part of a road safety package.

lemonde.title: Vincent Jeanbrun, ministre du logement : « Le défi est de mieux accompagner l’adaptation des logements aux pics de chaleur »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », le ministre expose les points-clés de son projet de loi destiné à augmenter l’offre d’habitations et présenté, mercredi, en conseil des ministres, et esquisse des pistes pour faire face aux canicules.

lemonde.title: Marc Bloch au Panthéon : revivez la cérémonie d’hommage à l’historien et résistant
lemonde.description: Quatre-vingt-deux ans après son exécution par la Gestapo, le 16 juin 1944, Marc Bloch est entré mardi 23 juin au Panthéon. Emmanuel Macron a honoré ses « enseignements qui nous obligent », contre « l’esprit de défaite ».

lemonde.title: Autonomie de la Corse : le principe a été approuvé par l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: C’est Gérald Darmanin, alors ministre de l’intérieur, qui avait été chargé par Emmanuel Macron de mettre sur pied le projet de loi, pour mettre un terme aux violences provoquées par la mort en prison du militant indépendantiste Yvan Colonna.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : la « loi intégrale » inscrite à l’agenda de l’Assemblée nationale, une victoire pour les féministes et les enfantistes
lemonde.description: Le texte, qui doit permettre de mieux lutter contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles, sera examiné à l’automne, a annoncé le premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, après un changement de pied. Un examen du Conseil d’Etat devrait cependant amener à changer les contours du projet de loi. Des arbitrages délicats restent à rendre, certains points mettant en porte à faux le garde des sceaux, Gérald Darmanin.

lemonde.title: Au Soudan, la crainte d’un assaut des paramilitaires sur El-Obeid
lemonde.description: Huit mois après la prise sanglante d’El-Fasher, la capitale du Kordofan du Nord pourrait à son tour tomber aux mains des Forces de soutien rapide. Depuis début juin, les paramilitaires mènent une intense campagne de bombardements aériens sur la ville.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Angleterre-Ghana : les Anglais ont la maîtrise du ballon, mais peinent à se montrer dangereux
lemonde.description: Impressionnants contre la Croatie, Harry Kane et ses coéquipiers ont l’occasion de valider dès ce soir leur billet pour les seizièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde. Mais les Ghanéens auront le même objectif.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le bilan des frappes russes de mardi s’élève à quatorze morts
lemonde.description: Six personnes ont été tuées, mardi, dans l’oblast de Dnipropetrovsk − trois dans la région de Nikpol, et trois dans la ville de Kryvy Rih. Les attaques russes du jour sur l’Ukraine ont aussi causé la mort de huit autres personnes, à Kherson, Odessa ou encore Sloviansk.

lemonde.title: Pesticides : condamné à réviser les autorisations de mise sur le marché, l’Etat propose de réévaluer sept produits, soit 0,28 % des tonnages utilisés
lemonde.description: Les associations à l’origine de l’affaire « Justice pour le vivant » vont de nouveau aller devant le tribunal pour dénoncer les « insuffisances » du plan d’action du gouvernement en matière d’évaluation des risques des pesticides, auquel « Le Monde » a eu accès.

lemonde.title: Loi de programmation militaire : les parlementaires s’accordent sur une hausse du budget des armées
lemonde.description: Sept députés et sept sénateurs se sont accordés sur une actualisation de la loi de programmation militaire. Leur mouture devra encore être adoptée le 30 juin au Sénat, puis le lendemain à l’Assemblée, Emmanuel Macron espérant la promulguer symboliquement avant le 14 juillet.

lemonde.title: Face à l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle, Cate Blanchett lance un site pour faire valoir les droits de chacun
lemonde.description: Présenté comme un « registre du consentement humain » par l’actrice australienne, ce portail en ligne propose à tout individu d’enregistrer les éléments qui forment son identité et d’autoriser ou d’interdire leur utilisation par les systèmes d’IA.

lemonde.title: « L’étagère du bas, c’est ma salle de bains » : le 10 mètres carrés parisien de Léa, toute jeune avocate
lemonde.description: « Et toi, t’habites où ? ». En pleine crise du logement, étudiants et jeunes actifs redéfinissent, souvent malgré eux, l’art de trouver un chez-soi. Cette semaine, Léa, 28 ans, originaire de Tours, raconte son attachement à son 10 mètres carrés, sans lequel elle n’aurait pas pu faire ses études de droit à la Sorbonne.

lemonde.title: Sylvie Gir, secrétaire générale des députés de droite et dernière chiraquienne de l’Assemblée, prend sa retraite
lemonde.description: Après quarante ans au Palais-Bourbon, la « SG » du groupe Droite républicaine sera remplacée par un proche de Laurent Wauquiez. Si elle n’était pas élue, elle a œuvré par conviction et fut une cheville ouvrière de la droite parlementaire.

lemonde.title: Consultation citoyenne de la Cour des comptes : l’engouement est là, les limites aussi
lemonde.description: La nouvelle campagne de participation citoyenne de la Rue Cambon s’est achevée lundi 22 juin : 1 096 sujets de contrôle et d’enquête ont été proposés par les citoyens. Une trentaine de thèmes devraient in fine être retenus par les juridictions financières pour nourrir de futurs « rapports d’initiative citoyenne ». L’exercice présente toutefois certaines limites.

lemonde.title: La mezzo-soprano Coline Dutilleul fait briller les étoiles dans le ciel noir de Schubert
lemonde.description: Avec « In deinen süssen Händen », la chanteuse belge livre un lumineux album où des lieder de Franz Schubert sur le thème de la mort voisinent avec des pièces pour clavier de Jean-Sébastien Bach.

lemonde.title: VIDEO Donald Trump critiqué après les travaux du bassin du Lincoln Memorial
lemonde.description: Ce gigantesque miroir d’eau est envahi par les algues et voit la peinture bleue du revêtement tout récemment posé se décoller. Les travaux voulus par le président américain s’élèvent à plus de 14 millions de dollars.

lemonde.title: Plusieurs établissements publics, dont Santé publique France, l’Anses et l’Ademe, manifesteront le 2 juillet
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement sert « les intérêts du privé » et détruit « pièce par pièce nos services publics en s’attaquant aux agences de l’Etat », selon Lise Soulier, représentante CGT à l’Institut national de l’information géographique et forestière.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : après sa défaite 2-3 face à la Norvège, le Sénégal est au bord de l'élimination
france24fr.description: La nuit a été cauchemardesque pour les supporters sénégalais après la défaite 3 buts à 2 des Lions de la Teranga face à la Norvège. Le Sénégal qui enchaîne une 2e défaite de suite dans cette entame de Coupe du monde et qui se met en danger pour une qualification au 2e tour.

france24fr.title: Marc Bloch au Panthéon : Macron salue son engagement contre "l'esprit de défaite"
france24fr.description: Quatre-vingt-deux ans après son exécution par la Gestapo, l'historien et résistant Marc Bloch a fait son entrée le 23 juin au Panthéon. Professeur spécialiste de l'histoire du Moyen Âge, combattant lors de la Première et de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, il n'a eu de cesse tout au long de sa vie de s'engager pour la France.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Didier Deschamps rentre en France suite au décès de sa mère et sera absent contre la Norvège
Mondial 2026 : Didier Deschamps rentre en France après le décès de sa mère
france24fr.description: Le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France Didier Deschamps a été endeuillé par le décès de sa mère et va rentrer en France pour assister à ses obsèques, a annoncé mardi la Fédération française de football (FFF), qui précise qu'il ne dirigera pas les Bleus contre la Norvège vendredi lors du dernier match du groupe de la France au Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: Comment la désinformation sexiste a envahi la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la Coupe du Monde, des vidéos de supportrices inondent les réseaux sociaux. Problème: elles sont toutes générées par l'Intelligence artificielle. Véhiculant une image hypersexualisée des femmes, elles permettent à leurs créateurs de gagner de l'argent grâce aux vues qu'elles génèrent. Décryptage dans Info Intox avec Jules BOITEAU.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Portugal se balade contre l'Ouzbékistan, doublé pour Cristiano Ronaldo
france24fr.description: La Seleçao n'a laissé aucune chance à l'Ouzbékistan (5-0), mardi 23 juin au stade de Houston, lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes. Le capitaine portugais Cristiano Ronaldo (41 ans) a ouvert le score dès la 6e minute, puis inscrit un doublé juste avant la pause (39e). Ces deux nouvelles réalisations font de lui le premier joueur de l'histoire à marquer lors de six Coupes du monde.

france24fr.title: Angleterre - Ghana en direct : les Three Lions toujours muets à la pause face aux Black Stars
france24fr.description: L'Angleterre et le Ghana s'affrontent au stade de Foxborough à 22 h (heure de Paris), à l'occasion de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes du Mondial 2026. Ce choc entre les Three Lions et les Black Stars, tous les deux victorieux lors de la première journée, sera déjà décisif pour la première place du groupe L. Suivez en direct le match commenté par nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Canicule : va-t-on enfin se réveiller ?
france24fr.description: Après des records de température enregistrés lundi et de nouveaux décès liés à la chaleur, la canicule exceptionnelle qui frappe la France s'étend encore un peu plus ce mardi. Les infrastructures et les organismes sont mis à rude épreuve. Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé un renforcement de la mobilisation du système de santé en activant le plan Orsan au niveau 2 sur 4.

france24fr.title: Canicule: la flore et la faune souffrent aussi de la chaleur
france24fr.description: La chaleur exceptionnelle de ce début d'été assèche les sols et entraîne une mortalité accrue de la végétation. Avec la multiplication de ces événements extrêmes, les écosystèmes migrent vers le nord. Les platanes et chênes ne peuvent pas survivre à ces coups de chaud répétés. Les animaux qui dépendent de ces arbres vont donc se déplacer là où ils peuvent survivre. La modification du climat est en train de transformer les paysages que nous connaissons.

france24fr.title: "Fimbu chicotte" : les origines du phénomène
france24fr.description: La RD Congo a démarré sa competition par un impressionnant match nul face au Portugal. Les Congolais ont célébré le but égalisateur par une danse iconique : Fimbu chicotte. Quelles sont les origines de cette chanson et pourquoi cette danse est-elle si populaire ?

france24fr.title: Ian Brossat (PCF) : "La canicule est une violence de classe"
france24fr.description: La France suffoque et bat des records de chaleur. Ian Brossat, sénateur PCF de Paris, estime que le gouvernement n’a pas pris de mesures concrètes et plaide pour "un grand plan national d’isolation des logements". Sur l’affaire Lyhanna, du nom de cette petite retrouvée morte le 4 juin dernier, le sénateur communiste considère qu’il "y a un sous-investissement dans la justice". Il revient aussi sur la présidentielle à venir et sur la place des communistes pour 2027.

france24fr.title: Calendrier, affiches et horaires : tout savoir sur les 16es de finale du Mondial 2026
france24fr.description: Les matches passent et on connaît désormais les premiers qualifiés pour la phase finale du Mondial 2026. Voici le calendrier complet des 16es de finale de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Canicule : la France connaît sa journée la plus chaude jamais enregistrée
france24fr.description: Mardi a été la journée "la plus chaude enregistrée en France" depuis le début des mesures en 1947, alors que de nombreux records absolus de température ont été battus dans l'ouest du pays, a indiqué Météo-France.

france24fr.title: J.D. Vance a-t-il été snobé par le Premier ministre qatari ?
france24fr.description: Sur les réseaux sociaux, une séquence tournée à Genève alimente des interprétations selon lesquelles le vice-président américain aurait été ignoré par le Premier ministre qatari. Mais les images ne racontent pas toute l’histoire.

france24fr.title: Comment Donald Trump s’est pris les pieds dans le bassin réfléchissant de Washington
france24fr.description: Le chantier de l'épuration de l'eau du célèbre bassin réfléchissant au pied du Lincoln Memorial à Washington est en train de tourner au cauchemar politique pour Donald Trump, qui s'y est personnellement investi. C'est une remise en cause de ses compétences premières : celles d'un magnat de l’immobilier censé savoir construire “une piscine”.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Tulsi Gabbard sous l'emprise d'une secte ? Les révélations du Washington Post
france24fr.description: L’ancienne cheffe du renseignement, Tulsi Gabbard, aurait-elle été influencée par une secte ? C'est ce qu'affirme une enquête publiée par le Washington Post. Les explications de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Les Fausses Notes du Brexit
france24fr.description:
Dix ans après le référendum qui a bouleversé le Royaume-Uni, quel est l'impact du Brexit sur l'une de ses plus grandes richesses : sa musique ?
 
De Liverpool à Paris, Sonia Patricelli part à la rencontre de celles et ceux qui font vivre la scène musicale britannique. Artistes confirmés, groupes émergents, producteurs et organisateurs de festivals racontent comment la sortie de l'Union européenne a transformé leur quotidien : tournées plus coûteuses, démarches administratives interminables, disp

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : la tour Eiffel ferme plus tôt que prévu
france24fr.description: La tour Eiffel a fermé ce mardi dès 16H00 et le musée du Louvre fera de même de mercredi jusqu'à samedi en raison de la canicule, ont annoncé leurs directions.

nzz.title: Deutschland: Bahnverkehr wegen Funkstörung bundesweit eingestellt
nzz.description: (dpa) Der Verkehr der Deutschen Bahn ist wegen einer Funkstörung bundesweit eingestellt. Das bestätigte ein Sprecher der Deutschen Bahn am Abend auf Anfrage der Nachrichtenagentur dpa. Vorläufig werden demnach alle Züge an Bahnhöfen zurückgehalten.

nzz.title: Die Zürcher FDP nominiert Andri Silberschmidt und Martin Huber für den Regierungsrat
nzz.description: An einer heissen Delegiertenversammlung haben die Freisinnigen den Neftenbacher Landwirt Martin Huber als zweiten Regierungsratskandidaten gekürt. Der Favorit Andri Silberschmidt wurde im ersten Wahlgang gewählt.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Sprit- und Gaspreise deutlich gesunken – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Cristiano Ronaldo führt Portugal zum Sieg
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: Wo sich die Hitze aushalten lässt: die schönsten Badis von Zürich
nzz.description: In Zürich ist das Wasser nie weit: Die Stadt ist so reich an Freibädern wie kaum eine andere in Europa. Wir zeigen die schönsten Anlagen.

nzz.title: Vermisstes Kind tot aus der Reuss geborgen
nzz.description: Dutzende von freiwilligen Helfern hatten tagelang nach einem Buben gesucht. Bei dem am Dienstag gefundenen Kind dürfte es sich um den vermissten 5-Jährigen handeln.

nzz.title: Wer ist der Beste, Messi oder Mbappé? Zwei Superstars kämpfen um die WM-Torjägerkrone
nzz.description: Die Weltmeisterschaft wird zum Generationenduell. Lionel Messi bricht den WM-Torrekord, doch Kylian Mbappé jagt ihn – die Zeit spielt für den Franzosen.

nzz.title: Versteckspiel um Taliban-Besuch bei der EU: Ohne Gegenleistungen wollen die Islamisten nicht über Ausschaffungen reden
nzz.description: Unter grosser Geheimhaltung sind Vertreter der afghanischen De-facto-Regierung nach Brüssel gereist. Die EU-Staaten sind auf ihre Mitarbeit angewiesen, wollen sie aber nicht diplomatisch anerkennen.

nzz.title: Zweifel an Unabhängigkeit und Unparteilichkeit: Das Bundesgericht setzt die Genfer Staatsanwaltschaft in einem Betrugsfall in den Ausstand
nzz.description: Die höchsten Richter haben der Verteidigung recht gegeben. Denn es geht um den Vater des Generalstaatsanwalts Olivier Jornot.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Weltschifffahrtsorganisation will 11.000 Seeleute evakuieren +++ Libanon und Israel verhandeln erneut in den USA
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Frische Idee für die Steuern: Überschüsse gehören den Bürgern
nzz.description: Der Kampf gegen die Steuer- und Abgabenlast ist ein urliberales Anliegen. Es ist erfreulich, dass die FDP das erkannt hat.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Nicht reden, sondern umsetzen: Die Rentenreform liefert die Chance, die Stimmung im Land zu drehen
nzz.description: Die Gremium hat geliefert, woran Vorgängerregierungen jahrzehntelang gescheitert sind. Kanzler Friedrich Merz könnte sich nun als echter Reformer profilieren – wenn er die nötige Durchsetzungskraft besitzt.

nzz.title: 15-Jähriger ertrinkt in der Limmat, ein Kollege filmt den Sprung und alarmiert die Polizei erst nach 27 Minuten
nzz.description: Ein 20-jähriger Angolaner steht wegen Unterlassung der Nothilfe vor dem Bezirksgericht Zürich. Die Staatsanwältin verlangt sechs Monate Freiheitsstrafe.

Nach dem Sportchef ist im EV Zug nun auch der CEO Geschichte – der Klub zerfleischt sich unter dem Präsidenten Hans-Peter Strebel selbst
nzz.description: Zerstritten, konzeptlos und sportlich mittelmässig: Der Meister von 2021 und 2022 hat in kürzester Zeit seine Glaubwürdigkeit verspielt.

zeit.description: Eine Funkstörung hat den Zugverkehr bundesweit zum Erliegen gebracht, S-Bahnen und Fernzüge können nicht weiterfahren. Laut der Bahn bleiben alle Züge an Bahnhöfen.

zeit.description: Im Spiel gegen Usbekistan hat Cristiano Ronaldo einen Meilenstein erreicht. Er ist der erste Spieler der Geschichte, der bei sechs Weltmeisterschaften getroffen hat.

observador.title: A locomotiva que virou TGV e encontrou os dois apeadeiros
observador.description: Nuno Mendes voltou a mostrar o porquê de ser provavelmente o melhor lateral do mundo e juntou-se a um eixo Bruno-Ronaldo que saiu da sombra e assumir o protagonismo: a análise à exibição da Seleção.

observador.title: França revela que morreu a mãe de Deschamps
observador.description: A FFF confirmou a ausência do selecionador, de 57 anos, no jogo de sexta-feira que decide os lugares no Grupo I. O adjunto Guy Stéphan assume o comando.

observador.title: As reações do Uzbequistão à derrota com Portugal
observador.description: Cannavaro já tinha avisado que o Mundial seria uma experiência de aprendizagem. Uzbequistão viu um golo seu ser anulado, o que abalou a confiança da equipa. No fim, sobraram as lágrimas de Khusanov.

observador.title: ONU reforça proteção dos "capacetes azuis"
observador.description: Resolução co-patrocinada por mais de 150 países quer melhorar investigações e julgamentos. Mais de 4.500 "capacetes azuis" morreram em serviço desde o início das missões da ONU.

observador.title: Martínez: "Estivemos muito consistentes até ao fim"
observador.description: Frente ao Uzbequistão, Roberto Martínez gostou da maturidade dos jogadores e realçou o exemplo Ronaldo. Selecionador falou de MacPhee, de Messi e perspetivou o jogo com a Colômbia.

observador.title: Regionalização. PCP leva ao Parlamento proposta de referendo
observador.description: PCP quer audições até ao fim do ano, municípios a pronunciarem-se sobre o mapa das regiões até junho de 2027 e eleição dos novos órgãos regionais em 2029. Governo não confirmou presença no debate.

observador.title: CM Lisboa tem 642 processos de ocupação abusiva por resolver
observador.description: O vereador Vasco Moreira Rato revelou na Assembleia Municipal que 548 dos 642 processos pendentes estão em fase final de análise. Novas ocupações têm ordem de desocupação imediata.

observador.title: Funcionários judiciais dizem trabalhar em "saunas"
observador.description: O Sindicato dos Funcionários Judiciais alerta para stress térmico em tribunais de norte a sul do país. Há casos sem climatização há cinco anos consecutivos.

observador.title: "Não deviam tê-lo irritado": imprensa reage a Ronaldo
observador.description: Depois de fortes críticas a Ronaldo, as manchetes internacionais sofreram uma reviravolta na narrativa em torno do jogador, com os principais analistas a renderem-se à capacidade do camisola 7.

observador.title: O inédito e passes de Vitinha e Bruno: os números da goleada
observador.description: Portugal goleou Uzbequistão para se estrear a ganhar no Mundial 2026 e colecionou registos positivos, entre a 3.ª maior goleada na prova, um resultado inédito ao intervalo e as assistências de Bruno.

observador.title: Ataques russos matam nove pesoas e fazem 30 feridos
observador.description: Mísseis e bombas aéreas russas atingiram Kryvii Rig, Nikopol, Zaporijia, Kherson e Odessa. Kiev responde com ofensiva de drones que ameaça cortar abastecimentos à Crimeia.

observador.title: O primeiro São João de Seguro como Presidente
observador.description: O chefe de Estado percorreu as Fontainhas, os Guindais e a ribeira com o presidente da Câmara. Recusou comentar o chumbo do pacote laboral: o foco era a festa e a Seleção.

observador.title: Portugal deve formar jovens para "economia que quer"
observador.description: "Numa economia em mudança estrutural, vamos ter sempre este desajuste em que estamos a formar pessoas para uma economia que ainda não temos exatamente, mas que queremos", afirmou Fernando Alexandre.

observador.title: As imagens da festa portuguesa contra o Uzbequistão
observador.description: Portugal voltou a entrar em campo e desta vez carimbou a primeira vitória no Mundial. Em Santos, em Lisboa, centenas de pessoas vibraram durante os 90 minutos e comemoraram os cinco golos da seleção.

observador.title: Israel não sai do Líbano sem que o Hezbollah seja desarmado
observador.description: António José Telo recorda que desarmamento do Hezbollah seria única solução para estabelecer paz minimamente estável no Líbano, mas é duvidoso que o grupo aceite.

observador.title: Austin MacPhee, o treinador de bolas paradas de Portugal
observador.description: O escocês de 46 anos acumula o trabalho no Aston Villa com o cargo de treinador adjunto na Seleção Nacional. No jogo com o Uzbequistão, Portugal já mostrou jogadas trabalhadas em livres e cantos.

observador.title: MNE da Rússia apelida Zelensky de "Fuehrer"
observador.description: Sergei Lavrov acusa o líder ucraniano de tentar envolver Bielorrússia no conflito. O chefe da diplomacia russa diz que Zelensky foi recrutado do teatro amador para desempenhar esse papel específico.

observador.title: Ucrânia destrói ponte ferroviária estratégica na Crimeia
observador.description: A agência Ukrinform revelou hoje que ataques com drones, em duas noites sucessivas, derrubaram a estrutura que era usada como uma via estratégica, tanto militar como logística, pela Rússia.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Bundesweiter Ausfall des Zugfunks legt Bahnverkehr lahm
spiegel.description: Bundesweite IT-Probleme bei der Bahn sorgen für erhebliche Einschränkungen im Zugverkehr. Nach Angaben des Konzerns sind interne Kommunikationssysteme betroffen, Züge werden aus Sicherheitsgründen zurückgehalten. Die Ursache ist unklar.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: England gegen Ghana im Liveticker
spiegel.description: Der Ball ist fast nur bei den von Thomas Tuchel trainierten Engländern. Aber Ghana verteidigt mit elf Spielern, die von der eigenen Querlatte baumeln, sehr effizient. Gelingt dem Favoriten der Durchbruch? Alles Wichtige im Livekommentar.

spiegel.title: Georgia Meloni setzt im Streit mit Donald Trump nun auf Deeskalation
spiegel.description: Trump behauptet, Meloni habe ihn beim G7-Gipfel um ein Foto angefleht. Ihre Reaktion? Deutlich und scharf – doch Italiens Regierungschefin will den Zwist jetzt offenbar nicht weiter ausufern lassen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Cristiano Ronaldo führt Portugal mit zwei Toren zu Sieg gegen Usbekistan
spiegel.description: Der verpatzte WM-Auftakt der Portugiesen wurde eng mit der schwachen Leistung Cristiano Ronaldos verknüpft. Gegen Usbekistan zeigte CR7 nun, dass er sein Ego zurückstellen kann – und schrieb Geschichte.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Bremer Schulklasse gerät bei Gewitter in Bergnot
spiegel.description: Gewitter sind in den Alpen eine echte Gefahr. Eine Schulklasse aus Deutschland geriet nun im Nachbarland durch Blitz und Donner in Bedrängnis. Ein Notruf folgte.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: Stichflamme beim Grillen – Elfjähriger rettet sich in Kanal
spiegel.description: Bei einem Grilltreffen in Niedersachsen ist ein Junge durch eine Stichflamme schwer verletzt worden. Um sich vor den Flammen zu retten, ist er ins Wasser gesprungen. Ein 17-Jähriger soll die Feuerflamme verursacht haben.

spiegel.title: Boris Pistorius: Der Verteidigungsminister will das Fregatten-Projekt F126 beenden
spiegel.description: SPD-Verteidigungsminister Pistorius plant, aus dem größten Rüstungsprojekt in der Geschichte der Marine auszusteigen. Der Schaden würde in die Milliarden gehen. Und auch die möglichen Ersatzkriegsschiffe werden teurer.

spiegel.title: Kenia: Proteste erzwingen Entschuldigung im Streit um Ebola-Zentrum
spiegel.description: Wochenlang haben Menschen in Kenia wegen eines Ebola-Isolierzentrums protestiert, das nur US-Amerikanern zugutekommen sollte. Ein Minister wollte das Projekt unbedingt durchdrücken – und musste sich jetzt entschuldigen.

spiegel.title: Gespräche mit Taliban: Vertreter erstmals in Brüssel empfangen
spiegel.description: Erstmals seit ihrer Rückkehr an die Macht sind Taliban zu Gesprächen in Brüssel empfangen worden. Die EU spricht von einem technischen Austausch über Abschiebungen nach Afghanistan – das Treffen steht jedoch in der Kritik.

spiegel.title: Straße von Hormus: Weltschifffahrtsorganisation will 11.000 festsitzende Seeleute evakuieren
spiegel.description: Für Tausende Seeleute an Bord von Tankern und Frachtern war die Blockade der Straße von Hormus eine besondere Belastung, sie saßen fest. Nun sollen sie nach Hause kommen.

spiegel.title: Korsika: Eine autonome Insel? Frankreichs Unterhaus billigt Pläne
spiegel.description: Das Verhältnis zwischen Paris und Ajaccio gilt als schwierig. Die Mittelmeerinsel will mehr Freiheiten. Frankreichs Nationalversammlung stimmt dem Wunsch zu, doch es gibt noch Hürden zu überwinden.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz und die Rente: Endlich mal ein guter Tag für den CDU-Kanzler
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler könnte Aufbruchstimmung verbreiten, Optimismus versprühen, aber es gelingt ihm nicht. Ein fast trauriger Ernst scheint ihn befallen zu haben, und er kann ihn nicht abschütteln.

spiegel.title: Frankreich, Spanien, Großbritannien: Hitze macht Europa zu schaffen
spiegel.description: Höchste Warnstufen in vielen Regionen: Eine beispiellose Hitzewelle hat weite Teile Europas erfasst. Frankreich meldete die heißeste Nacht seit Beginn der Wetteraufzeichnungen – einer von vielen Rekorden.

spiegel.title: Clueso: »Ich habe kein Problem damit, ›Fuck AfD‹ zu sagen«
spiegel.description: Er wurde in der DDR geboren, lebt in Erfurt und ist einer der populärsten deutschsprachigen Musiker: Clueso. Bei »DER SPIEGEL live« auf dem Hurricane-Festival spricht er über Haltung, KI und seinen Umgang mit Nazis im Kino.

spiegel.title: Herbert Grönemeyer erhält Deutschen Nationalpreis und kritisiert deutsche Politiker
spiegel.description: Herbert Grönemeyer hat den Deutschen Nationalpreis erhalten. In seiner Dankesrede rüffelt er die deutsche Spitzenpolitik, lobt die Zivilgesellschaft und sieht sich selbst in der Verantwortung.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Rentenreform, Lehrkräfte und Politik, Trumps Probleme mit dem Reflecting Pool in Washington
spiegel.description: Die Regierung legt ein innovatives Reformpaket vor – und bremst sich dabei nicht aus. Viele Lehrkräfte wissen nicht, was sie sagen dürfen. Und Donald Trump erlebt einen grünen Albtraum. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagabend.

spiegel.title: Rente – Frührente: Gartenbauer? Altenpflegerin? Wer die »Rente mit 63« wirklich nutzt
spiegel.description: Die Rente mit 63 soll laut einem Vorschlag der Expertenkommission gestrichen werden. Welche Berufsgruppen diese Entscheidung treffen dürfte – und welche Alternativen es geben soll.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Wer Felix Nmecha zusieht, der erkennt, was Deutschland kann und was nicht
spiegel.description: Mit seiner Technik und Wucht begeistert Felix Nmecha das Publikum und ist zum heimlichen deutschen Helden der WM aufgestiegen. Er vereint, was die DFB-Elf stark macht, steht aber auch für die deutschen Schwächen.

letemps.title: «On peut critiquer Macron, mais sur la politique mémorielle, il a été un bon président»: ce bilan fourni et bien vu d’Emmanuel Macron
letemps.description:

new-sci.description: Fans can make you hotter rather than cooler, but the temperature at which you should turn them off depends on several factors, including your age and the humidity level

new-sci.title: Elite Maya people had teeth placed in a cave far from their tombs
new-sci.description: A cave in Belize contains teeth from dozens of important Maya people buried elsewhere, which may attest to a ritual intended to ensure their passage to the underworld

new-sci.description: Raising children appears to keep the brain young, potentially acting as a buffer against cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s

new-sci.title: SpaceX's secretive plans to deliver cargo to Earth from space
new-sci.description: Not much is known about Starfall, SpaceX's new delivery system, but an assessment published in May revealed its intended purpose

new-sci.title: How some people's brains make an extraordinary recovery from stroke
new-sci.description: Around a third of people are able to almost fully rebuild their brains after a stroke and uncovering why is pointing the way to better treatments for everyone

new-sci.title: Unapproved gene therapy for boosting longevity is set to go on sale
new-sci.description: A gene therapy that instructs cells to produce more of an anti-ageing protein called klotho is about to be offered by a US company at overseas clinics to bypass FDA rules

new-sci.title: Woman with Alzheimer's starts conversing again after taking psilocybin
new-sci.description: A woman with severe Alzheimer's disease who hadn't spoken more than monosyllables in years began initiating conversation after a single dose of psilocybin

new-sci.title: New-to-science spider builds trap that flings ants into the air
new-sci.description: A spider living in the rainforests of Queensland, Australia, builds a snare trap reminiscent of a Roman-era ballista weapon that it uses to catapult green tree ants into a web 30 centimetres above

new-sci.title: How menopause radically changes the brain – and what happens after
new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: ‘Fusogenic’ neurosurgery let paralysed pigs walk again – are we next?
new-sci.description: Researchers say a surgery that let pigs with completely severed spinal cords walk again may lead to human trials, and then perhaps even full head or brain transplants. Columnist Helen Thomson is intrigued but sceptical of whether the technique can be successful in humans

new-sci.title: A promising natural technique to remove CO2 could backfire
new-sci.description: Several start-ups have tried to grow seaweed to remove atmospheric CO2, but this could affect the levels of nutrients in the ocean and hamper other CO2-sucking processes

new-sci.title: The surprising ways your brain changes from your 20s to your 40s
new-sci.description: When does your brain reach adulthood? We're now understanding the many ways the organ continues to mature decades after society first deems you an adult

new-sci.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
new-sci.description: The next generation of AI models are meant to be trained by people paid to have conversations with them, but several of these workers have admitted to New Scientist that they simply get chatbots to do it instead. This "AI inbreeding" may reduce the power and usefulness of future models, warn experts

new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: The one film to watch before seeing Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day
new-sci.description: With Steven Spielberg’s new extraterrestrial film Disclosure Day just out, it’s the ideal time to watch Close Encounters of the Third Kind – perhaps the perfect UFO film, says film columnist Bethan Ackerley

new-sci.title: Faecal transplant makes the brains of old mice act young again
new-sci.description: Older mice that received a faecal microbiome transplant from younger animals went on to have improved brain plasticity, which suggests their brains could overcome a neurological condition that is typically successfully treated only in childhood

phys-org.title: New energy-boosting quantum mechanism discovered in photosynthetic bacteria
phys-org.description: Researchers have discovered how certain photosynthetic bacteria use a sophisticated quantum mechanism to increase their efficiency when capturing sunlight. The study, published today in the journal Nature Chemistry and led by Professor Jenny Clark, reveals that nature has been using a process called "singlet fission," effectively a "two-for-one" energy deal, to optimize solar harvesting. The findings provide a new blueprint for green technology, particularly as engineers attempt to copy this mec

phys-org.title: New breakthrough spots deadly methanol without opening bottles
phys-org.description: A new optical technique developed by researchers at the University of St Andrews and Adelaide University allows toxic methanol in alcoholic spirits to be detected without opening the bottle. Published in the Journal of Physics: Photonics, this new work offers a powerful new tool for tackling counterfeit alcohol and improving consumer safety worldwide.

phys-org.title: Real-time imaging reveals 'RNA hub' driving adaptive immune response
phys-org.description: A lot of things need to go right on a molecular level for immune cells to launch an adaptive response to an infection. B cells can produce different classes of antibodies tailored for specific infections through controlled DNA damage and repair that alter the genetic information needed to encode the antibodies. When the process goes awry, it can produce mutations or genomic rearrangements that promote the formation of tumors.

phys-org.title: Controlling ice crystal growth using polymer nanoparticles
phys-org.description: Ice formation can damage biological samples, tissues and materials during freezing and thawing. In nature, specialized molecules known as ice-binding proteins prevent ice crystals from growing too large, helping organisms survive in extreme cold. Scientists have long tried to replicate this behavior using synthetic materials, but most designs have focused on how molecules interact with ice at their surface.

phys-org.title: Crop diversity and perennial grains could strengthen soil health under climate stress, study finds
phys-org.description: A McGill University study suggests that diversifying crops and replacing annual wheat with a perennial grain could help protect soil health as climate change brings more variable rainfall. The research is published in the journal Applied Soil Ecology.

phys-org.title: Moose are native to Colorado, study shows
phys-org.description: The modern Colorado moose is often considered just that: modern—brought to the state by wildlife officials in the late 1970s, preceded by very occasional reports of moose sightings in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

phys-org.title: Branched silver sensor offers more sensitive light-based drug measurements in blood plasma
phys-org.description: Medications can save lives, yet for some drugs, the concentration in a patient's bloodstream determines whether a treatment is effective or whether harmful side effects may occur. Researchers at the Leibniz Institute of Photonic Technology (Leibniz IPHT) in Jena, Germany, have developed a sensor surface capable of detecting drugs in blood plasma with high sensitivity while offering significantly greater stability than comparable silver-based surfaces. Their findings have been published in A

phys-org.title: Surprising diversity found among Europe's last Neanderthals
phys-org.description: A new study published in Nature provides the most detailed picture to date of Neanderthal diversity in Western Europe shortly before their extinction.

phys-org.title: People avoid loss, regret rather than rely on 'risk-return' financial strategy
phys-org.description: People make financial choices to avoid losing money or experiencing regret, rather than simply balancing expected monetary returns with their tolerance for financial risk, according to a new study led by Lisa Posey, associate professor of risk management in the Penn State Smeal College of Business.

phys-org.title: Webb pinpoints millions of stars within Cigar galaxy
phys-org.description: Located 12 million light-years away and undergoing rapid star formation, edge-on spiral galaxy Messier 82 (M82) is a scientifically unique sight to behold, and now NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has revealed previously unseen details.

phys-org.title: Plant protein pair reveals new wood-formation mechanism
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Biosciences Department at Durham University have discovered a previously unknown mechanism that helps plants control the formation of wood, a finding that could open new directions for research into plant growth, productivity and carbon storage. The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, reveals that two proteins on the surface of plant cells work together to regulate the cells that produce wood.

phys-org.title: DNA loops reveal how immune cells build millions of antibodies from one genome
phys-org.description: How does your body produce millions of antibodies from one genome? New research reveals how two closely related proteins help immune cells fold DNA, connecting distant genetic pieces to create diverse antibodies that help fend off disease.

phys-org.title: Light-based sensors detect extremely low levels of traumatic brain injury biomarkers
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a chip-based metasurface biosensor that can detect traumatic brain injury (TBI) biomarkers at extremely low levels. With further development, the technology could one day help doctors make a faster diagnosis after a head injury, helping to guide treatment and provide early warning when complications occur.

phys-org.title: Our ovary blueprint is ancient, according to sea stars
phys-org.description: At first glance, bat sea stars, the nubbly, orange, many-footed creatures often found on the seafloor, seem about as far from humans as one can get. Appearances can be deceiving, however. Scientists have found evidence showing human and sea star ovaries share similar genetics, cell types and signaling processes, despite their ancient evolutionary split. The research is published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Antibiotic resistance threatens vision in pets and horses, veterinary review warns
phys-org.description: Sight-threatening antibiotic-resistant eye infections are becoming a significant threat to vision in dogs, cats and horses, according to a new comprehensive review published in Veterinary Ophthalmology by researchers from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. The study examines global trends in antimicrobial resistance in animal eye infections and warns that multidrug-resistant bacteria are becoming more common in referral veterinary settings. The review also highlights a critical challenge for ve

phys-org.title: Horseshoe bats use echolocation to separate background echoes from those of fluttering prey
phys-org.description: Many bat species emit echolocation calls and use the returning echoes to find their way, detect the presence of fluttering insects, and locate and catch them. A new study investigated this behavior in greater horseshoe bats foraging in the wild. An international team, including researchers from the University of Tübingen, "flew" with bats via GPS recording tags with microphones.

phys-org.title: New infrastructure model prioritizes disaster spending for vulnerable cities
phys-org.description: A University of Houston engineering professor is helping cities, utilities and transportation agencies prepare for and recover from natural disasters. All these organizations face the same challenge: They know the next hurricane, flood, wildfire or other major disruption will occur, but they do not have enough resources to strengthen every vulnerable piece of infrastructure.

phys-org.title: How continental shelf seiches triggered flooding following New York and New Jersey hurricanes
phys-org.description: In 1938 and 1944, two major hurricanes struck Long Island, and after the initial winds subsided, the surges came back unexpectedly hours later, leading observers to wonder whether this was a tsunami. In a study appearing in Continental Shelf Research, scientists at Stevens Institute of Technology explain the phenomenon and warn that it could happen again.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.
